summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of antiphospholipid syndrome, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, epilepsy, and systemic lupus erythematosus was admitted for acute vertigo, diplopia, gait unsteadiness, and cognitive confusion. She reported gradual onset symptoms starting in the morning, including oscillopsia, hand tremor, and difficulty with task sequencing, which persisted despite meclizine use. A CT angiogram of the head and neck showed no acute stroke or vascular stenosis, with findings consistent with chronic small vessel disease. She underwent hemodialysis on hospital day 1, after which her symptoms improved. Urine analysis showed no infection. The neurology team concluded the episode was likely a vestibular or neurological event in the setting of her chronic conditions. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, advised to continue baseline medications including warfarin, resume dialysis, and follow up with her neurologist, with caution advised against driving until fully recovered.
